end.summary:
• Practised placing BCE and CE dates on a timeline.
• Aarav later ordered 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 CE, and 1947 CE correctly.
• Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
• The belief that one written source gives the whole truth remained at the end; it was not corrected after the last mention.
end.parentNote: Asha used a drawn timeline to practise that BCE years move down toward 1 BCE and CE years move forward. Aarav correctly gave the sequence 3000 BCE, 500 BCE, 100 CE, and 1947 CE later in the lesson. The mix-up about trusting one stone inscription or book completely was still present at the end. At home, place a few BCE and CE dates on a hand-drawn line and discuss what two different sources might each tell us.
